pool.text: Rouen received its founding charter permitting self‑government.
King Philip II entered Rouen, annexing Normandy to France.
Mayor of Rouen was assassinated during urban strife.
Rouennais repurchased their old liberties and charter.
King Philip IV expelled the Jewish community of Rouen.
The Harelle urban revolt erupted among the underclass.
Rouen severely damaged by bombing wave.
Rouen hosted the French Grand Prix at Rouen‑Les‑Essarts track.
Rouen twinned with Norwich, England, United Kingdom.
Rouen twinned with Baton Rouge, Louisiana, United States.
Rouen twinned with Hannover, Germany.
Archaeological site discovered, later became a museum.
Rouen twinned with Zhejiang, China.
Rouen twinned with Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland.
Rouen authorities demolished grandstands of its racing past.
Rouen twinned with Salerno, Italy.
Museum of Natural History re‑opened after renovation.
Rouen twinned with Cleveland, Ohio, United States.
Rouen Impressionnée installed Arne Quinze’s sculpture ‘Camille’.
Rouen’s seaport merged with Le Havre and Paris to form HAROPA Port.
